# InkCanvas

Header: `winui/ui/media/InkCanvas.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/InkCanvas.hpp`.

A surface the user draws ink on with the pointer.

In Inking mode a press starts a stroke, every move adds a point and the release commits it to [strokes()](#strokes), raising [on_strokes_collected()](#on_strokes_collected). A press without a move leaves a dot. The stroke is drawn as it grows, each point at the pen's pressure. A mouse always reports 0.5. In Erasing mode the drag removes each stroke it passes over and raises [on_strokes_erased()](#on_strokes_erased). A pen's eraser end or eraser button does the same in Inking mode, unless set_eraser_input_enabled(false) turns it off. With `fit_to_curve`, strokes are smoothed into Bézier curves. Highlighter strokes are drawn first and translucent, the rest on top, all clipped to the canvas. The canvas has no background of its own, so put it in a [ui::BorderControl](../layout/border.md#uibordercontrol) for paper.

Only the devices in [input_device_types()](#input_device_types) draw. By default these are the pen and the mouse, which leaves touch to whatever scrolls the canvas. A right-button drag, including a pen with its barrel button held, draws nothing and goes to [on_unprocessed_input()](#on_unprocessed_input) (see [set_right_drag_action()](#set_right_drag_action)). So does every press, move and release in None mode. Use that input to build a lasso or another tool of the app's own. A ruler and a protractor, shown with [set_ruler()](#set_ruler) and [set_protractor()](#set_protractor), lie over the ink to draw straight lines and arcs along. With set_erase_mode(InkCanvasEraseMode::Point) the eraser removes only the ink under it, [eraser_size()](#eraser_size) wide, and leaves the rest of a stroke it crosses as new strokes. [strokes()](#strokes) is the data to save, in whatever format the app likes. [`ui::InkCanvas`](#uiinkcanvas) is the declarative form, and [ui::InkToolbarControl](ink-toolbar.md#uiinktoolbarcontrol) is a ready-made set of tools for it.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  owned  = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
auto* canvas = owned.get();
canvas->set_drawing_attributes({.color = ui::Color::from_rgba(230, 27, 27), .size = {4.0f, 4.0f}});
canvas->on_strokes_collected([](std::span<const ui::InkStroke> added)
                             { std::println("{} new stroke(s)", added.size()); });
window.set_content(std::move(owned));

canvas->set_input_mode(ui::InkCanvasInputMode::Erasing); // the next drag erases
canvas->strokes().clear();                                // or wipe it all
```

## `ui::InkCanvas`

A surface the user draws ink on. Builds a [ui::InkCanvasControl](#uiinkcanvascontrol), whose description says what the pointer does in each mode.

[`strokes`](#uiinkcanvas-strokes) is the drawing it starts with. Read and change the strokes later through the control's [InkCanvasControl::strokes()](#strokes). The canvas has no background of its own, so it usually sits in a [ui::Border](../layout/border.md#uiborder).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::InkCanvas> canvas;
ui::Property<std::size_t>  count{0};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
    ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(count, [](std::size_t n) { return std::format("{} stroke(s)", n); })},
    ui::Border{
        .background       = ui::colors::White,
        .border_brush     = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 0, 0, 40),
        .border_thickness = ui::Thickness{1.0f},
        .height           = 280.0f,
        .content          = ui::InkCanvas{
            .drawing_attributes = ui::InkDrawingAttributes{.color = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 77, 230),
                                                           .size  = {4.0f, 4.0f}},
            .accessibility      = {.name = "Drawing canvas"},
            .on_strokes_changed = [&] { count = canvas->strokes().size(); },
            .control            = canvas,
        },
    },
    ui::Button{.text = "Clear", .on_click = [&] { canvas->strokes().clear(); }},
}});
```

### on_unprocessed_input

```cpp
void on_unprocessed_input(Callback<void(const PointerEvent&)> handler)
```

Raised for pointer input the canvas doesn't turn into ink, with the position in canvas DIPs. In None mode that is every press, move and release over the canvas, plus the moves of a drag that left it. In the other modes it is a right-button drag, from press to release, when the right-drag action is InkCanvasRightDragAction::LeaveUnprocessed. A Leave event ends a drag the window lost.

### enabled_changed

```cpp

```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

## class InkStrokeContainer

The strokes on a [ui::InkCanvasControl](#uiinkcanvascontrol). Read them, add, remove, clear or replace them all, and select, move and delete some of them.

Every stroke that goes in gets a fresh `id` in place of the one it came with, so a set saved with [strokes()](#strokes) and handed back to [replace()](#replace) comes back renumbered. Every change, including a change of selection, redraws the canvas and raises [InkCanvasControl::on_strokes_changed()](#on_strokes_changed). Each canvas owns one container, reached through [InkCanvasControl::strokes()](#strokes).

Selection is the basis for a lasso. The canvas reports the pointer input it doesn't turn into ink through [InkCanvasControl::on_unprocessed_input()](#on_unprocessed_input). The app collects the outline, passes it to [select_with_polyline()](#select_with_polyline), then moves or deletes the selected strokes.

Example: 
```cpp
// Keep a copy, clear the canvas, and put the drawing back later.
auto canvas = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
std::vector<ui::InkStroke> saved{canvas->strokes().strokes().begin(), canvas->strokes().strokes().end()};
canvas->strokes().clear();
canvas->strokes().replace(std::move(saved));
```


## struct InkStroke

One stroke of ink: its points, in drawing order, and how it looks.

A stroke is a plain value. A [ui::InkStrokeContainer](#class-inkstrokecontainer) gives it an [`id`](#id) when it is added.

Example: 
```cpp
auto          canvas = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
ui::InkStroke tick{.points = {{.position = {20, 50}}, {.position = {40, 70}}, {.position = {80, 20}}}};
tick.attributes.color = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 128, 85);
canvas->strokes().add_stroke(std::move(tick));
```

### points

```cpp
std::vector<InkPoint> points {}
```

The sampled points, in canvas DIPs.

### attributes

```cpp
InkDrawingAttributes attributes {}
```

[Color](../core/color.md), size, nib and the rest.

### id

```cpp
std::uint32_t id = 0
```

Unique within its container. 0 for a stroke in no container.

### selected

```cpp
bool selected = false
```

Whether the stroke is selected. A selected stroke is drawn hollow in its own color, and the container's move_selected() and delete_selected() act on it.

### bounding_rect

```cpp
Rect bounding_rect() const
```

The area the stroke paints: its points' bounds grown by half the nib at its widest. An empty rect at the origin for a stroke with no points.

## struct InkPoint

One sampled point of an ink stroke: where it is, in the canvas's own DIPs (0,0 is the canvas's top-left corner), and how hard the pen pressed there.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::InkStroke line;
line.points = {{.position = {10, 10}}, {.position = {90, 40}, .pressure = 0.9f}};
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `Point` |  | [Canvas](../layout/canvas.md#uicanvas) DIPs. |
| `pressure` | `float` | `0.5f` | 0 to 1, the pen's [PointerEvent::pressure](../core/pointer-event.md). A mouse always reports 0.5. |

## struct InkDrawingAttributes

How a stroke looks. The defaults are a black, round, 2 DIP pen.

[`size`](#size) is the nib's width and height. A pressure-sensitive stroke scales it at each point: a quarter of the size at no pressure, the full size at 0.5 and 1.75 times the size at full pressure. [`ignore_pressure`](#ignore_pressure) keeps every point at the full size. A highlighter is drawn at half opacity and under the ordinary ink, so writing stays legible over it.

Example: 
```cpp
auto canvas = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
ui::InkDrawingAttributes marker{
    .color               = ui::Color::from_rgba(255, 230, 0),
    .size                = {6.0f, 18.0f},
    .pen_tip             = ui::InkPenTip::Rectangle,
    .draw_as_highlighter = true,
};
canvas->set_drawing_attributes(marker);
```

```cpp
Color color = colors::Black
```


```cpp
float pencil_opacity = 1.0f
```

Opacity from 0 to 1, for pencil ink only.

### for_pencil

```cpp
static InkDrawingAttributes for_pencil()
```

The defaults with [`kind`](#kind) set to Pencil.

## struct InkRuler

The ruler on a [ui::InkCanvasControl](#uiinkcanvascontrol), a straight edge to draw along.

While it shows, a press on its body drags it and the wheel over it turns it. A stroke started on or close outside one of its long edges is drawn straight along that edge, outside it, wherever the pointer goes. Its scale is in centimeters, at 96 DIPs to the inch, and it shows its angle.

Example: 
```cpp
auto canvas = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
canvas->set_ruler({.visible = true, .angle = 30.0f}); // centered on the canvas, turned 30 degrees
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `bool` | `false` | Shown on the canvas. |
| `center` | `std::optional<Point>` |  | Its middle, canvas DIPs. nullopt is the canvas's center. |
| `angle` | `float` | `0.0f` | Degrees clockwise from horizontal. |
| `length` | `float` | `600.0f` | Its length, DIPs. |
| `width` | `float` | `80.0f` | Its width across, DIPs. |
| `tick_marks` | `bool` | `true` | The centimeter scale. |

## struct InkProtractor

The protractor on a [ui::InkCanvasControl](#uiinkcanvascontrol), a circle to draw arcs along.

While it shows, a press on its body drags it and the wheel over it turns its scale. A stroke started on or close outside its edge is drawn around the circle, outside it.

Example: 
```cpp
auto canvas = std::make_unique<ui::InkCanvasControl>();
canvas->set_protractor({.visible = true, .center = ui::Point{200, 150}, .radius = 120.0f});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `bool` | `false` | Shown on the canvas. |
| `center` | `std::optional<Point>` |  | Its center, canvas DIPs. nullopt is the canvas's center. |
| `angle` | `float` | `0.0f` | How far the scale is turned clockwise, degrees. |
| `radius` | `float` | `160.0f` | Its radius, DIPs. |
| `tick_marks` | `bool` | `true` | A degree scale around the edge. |
| `center_marker` | `bool` | `true` | A cross at the center. |
| `angle_readout` | `bool` | `true` | A readout of its angle under the center. |

## Enumerations

### InkPenTip

```cpp
enum class InkPenTip
```

The shape of the nib a stroke is drawn with.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Circle` | A round nib, elliptical when its width and height differ. Draws smooth, even lines. |
| `Rectangle` | A flat, axis-aligned nib, like a highlighter's chisel tip. |

### InkDrawingAttributesKind

```cpp
enum class InkDrawingAttributesKind
```

Which family of ink a stroke's attributes describe.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Default` | Pen and highlighter ink. |
| `Pencil` | Pencil ink: lighter, with a grain of specks, at `pencil_opacity`. |

### InkCanvasInputMode

```cpp
enum class InkCanvasInputMode
```

What pointer input on a [ui::InkCanvasControl](#uiinkcanvascontrol) does.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Draws and erases nothing. Pointer input goes to on_unprocessed_input(). |
| `Inking` | The default. A drag draws a stroke with drawing_attributes(), and a pen's eraser erases. |
| `Erasing` | A left-button drag removes every whole stroke it touches (the stroke eraser). |

### InkCanvasRightDragAction

```cpp
enum class InkCanvasRightDragAction
```

What a right-button drag on a [ui::InkCanvasControl](#uiinkcanvascontrol) does. A pen pressed with its barrel button held counts as the right button.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `LeaveUnprocessed` | The default. The drag isn't inked and goes to on_unprocessed_input(). |
| `AllowProcessing` | Inks or erases as a left-button drag does. |

### InkCanvasEraseMode

```cpp
enum class InkCanvasEraseMode
```

What the eraser removes.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Stroke` | The default. Every whole stroke the eraser touches. |
| `Point` | Only the ink under the eraser. A stroke it crosses splits in two. |
